items.answer:
For a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd recommend **Apollo.io** as your single AI SDR and prospecting vendor.

## Why Apollo.io fits this situation best

- **All-in-one stack**: Apollo combines a large B2B contact database, AI enrichment, sequencing (email + LinkedIn + calls), and basic CRM-like pipeline tracking in one platform. For a small team with zero SDRs, this avoids stitching together multiple tools (data + sending + research). [monday](https://monday.com/blog/crm-and-sales/best-ai-sdr-tools/)
- **Strong for SMB / price-sensitive teams**: Independent comparisons explicitly call out Apollo as the best fit for "SMB or price-sensitive teams needing broad reach," thanks to its generous entry tier and breadth of functionality per dollar. [origami](https://origami.chat/blog/best-ai-sales-prospecting-tools-startups-small-businesses-2026)
- **Fast time to first lead**: In "speed to first lead" tests, Apollo consistently passes: a new rep can get a usable prospect list quickly without needing a technical person to build complex workflows (unlike Clay). [origami](https://origami.chat/blog/best-ai-sales-prospecting-tools-startups-small-businesses-2026)
- **Good ICP coverage for mainstream SaaS**: If your ICP is typical mid-market or enterprise tech/SaaS, Apollo's data coverage is strong enough to support meaningful outbound without immediate need for premium data vendors. [origami](https://origami.chat/blog/best-ai-sales-prospecting-tools-startups-small-businesses-2026)
- **AI features aligned with early-stage needs**: Apollo offers AI-assisted prospecting, messaging suggestions, and intent signals that help a small team approximate an SDR function without hiring immediately. [marblism](https://www.marblism.com/blog/what-are-the-best-ai-tools-for-sales-prospecting)

## How I'd use it as VP of Sales in your scenario

- Start with **one seat** for the founder/early seller, define a clear ICP in Apollo, and run 1–2 simple sequences (email + LinkedIn) to validate messaging and response rates. [origami](https://origami.chat/blog/best-ai-sales-prospecting-tools-startups-small-businesses-2026)
- Use Apollo's built-in data and filters instead of buying separate data tools; layer in light personalization via AI message suggestions rather than over-engineering at this stage. [origami](https://origami.chat/blog/best-ai-sales-prospecting-tools-startups-small-businesses-2026)
- As pipeline grows, add a second seat and consider integrating Apollo with your CRM, but keep the core stack unified to avoid tool sprawl on a 20-person team. [monday](https://monday.com/blog/crm-and-sales/best-ai-sdr-tools/)

If you later outgrow Apollo (e.g., you want fully autonomous AI SDR agents), you can evaluate more specialized AI SDRs like 11x.ai, Artisan, or AiSDR, but for a 20-person startup with no SDRs today, Apollo gives the best balance of coverage, ease of use, and cost. ## Shortlist b
items.answer:
If you're moving off 11x, don't evaluate only "another AI SDR." First decide whether you want **autonomous outbound**, **human-led sales engagement**, or a **modular prospecting stack**. My shortlist would be **Regie.ai, Artisan, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, and Clay**, with the right choice depending on your team size, CRM, channel mix, and tolerance for automation risk.

## Shortlist by operating model

| Option | Best fit | What to evaluate |
|---|---|---|
| **Regie.ai / RegieOne** | Closest replacement if you still want AI-led prospecting | Autonomous prospect discovery, enrichment, personalized outreach, calls, LinkedIn workflows, CRM logging, and human handoff. Regie positions its agents as handling discovery through outreach across multiple channels. [regie](https://www.regie.ai/prospecting-agents) |
| **Artisan** | Direct AI-BDR alternative | Quality of research, email personalization, deliverability, objection handling, meeting booking, and how much human control managers retain. |
| **Apollo** | Cost-conscious teams wanting data plus execution in one platform | Contact-data accuracy in your ICP, sequencing, dialer, enrichment, CRM sync, and total cost. Apollo combines prospecting data and sales engagement rather than requiring several separate tools. [apollo](https://www.apollo.io/) |
| **Outreach** | Larger or process-heavy sales organizations | Governance, forecasting, coaching, deal management, permissions, analytics, and enterprise integrations. Outreach now combines engagement, deal management, forecasting, coaching, and AI agents. [outreach](https://www.outreach.io/product) |
| **Salesloft** | Teams focused on rep execution and manager visibility | Cadences, next-best actions, conversation intelligence, coaching, forecasting, and AI-assisted research. Salesloft's AI agents are designed to prioritize actions, research accounts, identify buyers, and support sellers. [salesloft](https://www.salesloft.com/platform/ai-agents) |
| **Clay + your preferred sequencer** | RevOps teams wanting maximum control and data flexibility | Enrichment waterfalls, signal quality, workflow maintenance, cost per enriched record, and integration with your CRM and engagement tool. Clay supports enrichment from many providers and routing qualified prospects into the sales workflow. [clay](https://www.clay.com/blog/how-to-create-your-own-sales-prospect-list-in-minutes) |

## My practical recommendation

- **Want the closest strategic substitute for 11x:** Pilot **Regie.ai and Artisan**.
- **Want lower cost and faster implementation:** Evaluate **Apollo**.
- **Want to put humans back in control while improving execution:** Evaluate **Salesloft or Outreach**.
- **Have strong RevOps capability and unusual ICP signals:** Build a controlled stack around **Clay**, your CRM, and a sequencer.
- **Have enterprise governance, multiple sales teams, or complex forecasting requirements:** Start with **Outreach and Salesloft**, not a standalone AI SDR.

I would avoid replacing 11x with another black-box agent unless the vendor can show exactly **why each prospect was selected, what data informed the message, when a sequence pauses, and how a rep takes over**.

## Evaluation scorecard

Weight the evaluation around outcomes rather than feature count:

| Category | Suggested weight | Questions to ask |
|---|---:|---|
| Pipeline quality | 25% | Does it create qualified opportunities, not merely replies or meetings? |
| Data quality | 15% | What are email accuracy, role accuracy, firmographic freshness, and duplicate rates in your ICP? |
| Deliverability and compliance | 15% | How does it protect domains, manage opt-outs, respect regional rules, and detect risky sending patterns? |
| CRM and workflow fit | 15% | Does it write cleanly to Salesforce or HubSpot, preserve attribution, and prevent duplicate touches? |
| Control and explainability | 10% | Can managers approve messaging, set guardrails, inspect reasoning, and stop campaigns immediately? |
| Rep and manager usability | 10% | Does it reduce work without creating another queue of bad meetings and exceptions? |
| Economics | 10% | Calculate cost per qualified opportunity and cost per pipeline dollar—not just license price. |

## Run a controlled pilot

Give each finalist the same:

1. ICP and exclusions.
2. Target-account list.
3. Approved positioning, proof points, and disallowed claims.
4. Suppression list and existing customer records.
5. Meeting qualification criteria.
6. Two to four weeks of execution time.

Measure **qualified meetings held, opportunity conversion, pipeline created, positive-reply rate, bounce rate, unsubscribe/complaint rate, rep time required, and CRM-data accuracy**. Require the vendor to report results by segment, persona, message, and channel; otherwise, you won't know whether the tool works or merely found an easy pocket of prospects.

## The key decision

The most important question is: **Are you replacing an SDR, replacing an outbound stack, or replacing a workflow?**

If you need predictable enterprise execution, choose a governed platform such as Outreach or Salesloft. If you need autonomous top-of-funnel coverage, test Regie and Artisan. If you primarily need better targeting and data while keeping your team's process, Apollo or Clay may be the better transition. Claims about AI SDR performance are often vendor-supplied, so make your own pilot results the deciding evidence.

items.prompt: I'm a SDR manager. Best AI sales prospecting and outbound platforms for a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team with GDPR compliance for UK and EU prospect data.
items.snippet: For a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd choose **Apollo + HubSpot** for the best balance of AI prospecting, sequencing, CRM, and cost. If UK/EU data compliance is your highest priority, choose **Cognism or Dea
items.answer:
For a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd choose **Apollo + HubSpot** for the best balance of AI prospecting, sequencing, CRM, and cost. If UK/EU data compliance is your highest priority, choose **Cognism or Dealfront for data**, then use a controlled outreach tool such as **Lemlist** rather than relying on an autonomous AI SDR.

## Best platforms

| Platform | Best for | Strengths | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Apollo.io** | Best all-in-one startup option | Prospect database, AI research, enrichment, sequences, dialer, CRM integrations, affordable entry point | US-based provider; you must review international transfers, source provenance, and lawful-basis documentation |
| **Cognism** | Highest-confidence UK/EU prospect data | Strong UK and European coverage, phone verification, TPS/CTPS and other do-not-call screening, privacy and DSAR processes | Usually quote-based and more expensive; still requires a separate CRM and engagement workflow |
| **Dealfront** | Europe-first and EU-hosted prospecting | European company data, website visitor identification, intent signals, public-register sourcing, EU-focused privacy posture | Less suitable if you need a fully built-in multichannel outbound engine |
| **Lemlist** | Compliant, personalized outbound execution | Email sequences, AI personalization, multichannel workflows, DPA, EEA data storage according to its documentation | It is primarily an engagement layer, so data quality depends on your data provider |
| **Clay** | Advanced enrichment and custom AI workflows | Connects multiple data providers, supports AI research and personalization, highly flexible | Compliance depends on every connected data source and subprocessor; not ideal as the first tool for a team with no SDR process |
| **Outreach or Salesloft** | Mature enterprise sales operations | Strong governance, sequencing, analytics, coaching, and CRM controls | Generally excessive cost and complexity for a 20-person startup without SDRs |

Apollo documents UK/EU notices, opt-out controls, DPA terms, data-subject workflows, and the ability to exclude EU contacts from prospecting and emailing. That makes it a practical startup choice, but not an automatic legal solution. [knowledge.apollo](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409141087757-General-Data-Protection-Regulation-GDPR-Overview)

Cognism states that it screens telephone data against UK TPS/CTPS and other national do-not-call lists, performs privacy assessments, supports DSARs, and maintains GDPR-related documentation. Dealfront states that it uses a legitimate-interest basis for business contact data and provides a DPA, while positioning itself around European data sources. [help.cognism](https://help.cognism.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406236439826-What-has-Cognism-done-internally-to-comply-with-GDPR-and-data-privacy-regulations)

## My recommended stack

### Option 1: Best overall

**Apollo + HubSpot CRM + Google Workspace/Microsoft 365**

Use Apollo to identify accounts, find contacts, generate research briefs, and run small, carefully targeted sequences. Keep HubSpot as the system of record for lifecycle stages, suppression lists, replies, opportunities, and unsubscribe status.

This is the simplest option when nobody has yet built an SDR process. Start with a small number of high-fit accounts rather than immediately sending thousands of emails.

### Option 2: Best for UK/EU compliance

**Dealfront or Cognism + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Dealfront when EU hosting, European company data, and source traceability matter most. Use Cognism when verified UK/EU phone data and country-specific telephone screening are especially important. Send campaigns through Lemlist, whose documentation describes a GDPR DPA and EEA storage. [lemlist](https://www.lemlist.com/de/legal/dpa)

This stack costs more and involves more integrations, but it separates **data quality** from **outreach execution**, making vendor and compliance reviews clearer.

### Option 3: Best for sophisticated personalization

**Cognism or Apollo + Clay + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Clay only after your ICP, messaging, suppression rules, and review process are working. It is powerful for combining firmographic, technographic, hiring, funding, and website signals, but every connected provider must be assessed individually; Clay's DPA does not make all external data sources compliant by itself. [explore.openli](https://explore.openli.com/privacy/clay-3/data-processing-agreements)

## GDPR and UK outreach requirements

"GDPR-compliant platform" does not mean every campaign sent through it is lawful. Your company remains responsible for the purpose, lawful basis, targeting, message, retention, and handling of objections.

For UK campaigns, the ICO says that marketing to corporate subscribers by email generally does not require PECR consent, but you still need a valid UK GDPR lawful basis—often legitimate interests—and must distinguish corporate subscribers from sole traders and certain partnerships. The ICO also says legitimate interests is not automatic: you must complete the three-part test and comply with other marketing laws. [ico.org](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)

For EU campaigns, document a legitimate-interest assessment, explain who you are and why you are contacting the person, provide an immediate objection/unsubscribe method, minimize stored data, and maintain a suppression list. The EDPB describes legitimate interest as requiring a legitimate purpose, necessity, and a balancing test against the individual's rights. [edpb.europa](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-adopts-opinion-on-processors-guidelines-on-legitimate-interest-statement-on-draft_en)

## Minimum operating controls

Before sending, configure:

- Country and subscriber-type rules, especially for sole traders and individual professionals.
- A documented legitimate-interest assessment for each campaign or market.
- Vendor DPA, subprocessor list, international-transfer mechanism, retention terms, and deletion process.
- Source and collection date for each contact.
- Privacy notice link or first-touch transparency wording.
- One-click unsubscribe and a central, permanent suppression list.
- TPS/CTPS screening for UK phone outreach and equivalent national registers where applicable.
- Human approval for AI-generated claims, personalization, and contact selection.
- Conservative limits: for example, start with 20–40 highly relevant new contacts per sender per day and monitor complaints, bounces, and positive replies.

## Final choice

I would shortlist **Apollo**, **Cognism**, and **Dealfront** for evaluation:

1. **Apollo** if budget, speed, and an all-in-one workflow matter most.
2. **Cognism** if UK/EU contact quality and compliance evidence justify a premium price.
3. **Dealfront** if European data residency, public-register sourcing, and intent signals are central.

For your situation, the most sensible pilot is **Apollo + HubSpot for 30 days**, with a compliance review before launch. If Apollo's UK/EU data coverage or legal documentation is not sufficient, move to **Cognism or Dealfront for the data layer** and keep **Lemlist** for controlled execution.

items.prompt: I'm a SDR manager. 11x vs AiSDR — which is better for a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team?
items.snippet: For a **20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd choose AiSDR first—not 11x**. AiSDR is cheaper, faster to launch, and better suited to validating your outbound motion before committing to an enterprise-style autonom
items.answer:
For a **20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd choose AiSDR first—not 11x**. AiSDR is cheaper, faster to launch, and better suited to validating your outbound motion before committing to an enterprise-style autonomous sales system. Its official plans start at $250/month, with the commonly positioned Explore plan at $900/month billed quarterly; 11x's Alice starts at $3,750/month billed annually, or $36,000/year. [aisdr](https://aisdr.com/pricing/)

## Quick comparison

| Factor | AiSDR | 11x |
|---|---|---|
| Best fit | Startups and SMBs testing outbound | Larger teams scaling an established outbound engine |
| Starting cost | From $250/month; Explore commonly listed at $900/month | $3,750/month, billed annually |
| Commitment | Monthly/quarterly options depending on plan | Annual commitment on Growth |
| Primary strength | Research-led, relatively accessible outbound | More autonomous, multi-channel sales execution |
| Operational burden | You still need to define ICP, messaging, and qualification | More vendor-led implementation and oversight |
| Main risk | Limited depth if your motion becomes complex | High cost and over-automation before product-market/message fit |

11x has broader enterprise-oriented capabilities and supports more extensive autonomous outreach, but its pricing and annual commitment make it a significant bet for a company that has not yet built an SDR process. [11x](https://www.11x.ai/products/alice/pricing)

## Why AiSDR is the better first move

At your size, the main problem probably isn't sending more messages—it's discovering:

- Which customer segment responds.
- Which pain point creates meetings.
- Which titles are genuine buyers.
- What qualification criteria define a good opportunity.
- Whether outbound can produce pipeline at an acceptable cost.

AiSDR's lower entry price lets you test those assumptions without spending roughly $45,000 in the first year on the base 11x Growth plan. AiSDR also advertises research-led personalization, email/LinkedIn/call outreach, and approximately 1–3 meetings per 100 leads; treat those meeting figures as a vendor claim that must be validated against your own data. [aisdr](https://aisdr.com/)

## When 11x makes sense

Choose 11x instead if most of these are already true:

- You have a clearly defined ICP and repeatable messaging.
- Your average contract value is high enough to justify a large annual commitment.
- You want autonomous execution across several channels, potentially including voice.
- Someone on the team can manage deliverability, compliance, routing, and meeting quality.
- You already know the economics of a qualified meeting and opportunity.

In other words, **11x is a scale decision; AiSDR is a learning and validation decision**.

## Recommended rollout

I'd run AiSDR as a controlled 6–8 week pilot:

1. Pick one narrow ICP, one geography, and one buyer persona.
2. Start with 300–500 carefully selected accounts rather than maximum volume.
3. Have the founder, CEO, or sales manager approve the first campaigns and replies.
4. Track positive-reply rate, qualified-meeting rate, show rate, opportunity rate, and pipeline generated—not just meetings booked.
5. Continue only if the resulting opportunities meet your target customer profile and economics.

Do not let either tool operate as an unsupervised replacement for sales strategy. With no SDR team, assign one internal owner—probably the founder, sales leader, or growth marketer—to review targeting, replies, and qualification every week.

**Verdict:** Start with **AiSDR**, preferably on the lowest plan that supports a meaningful test. Reconsider 11x after you have proven your ICP, messaging, deliverability, and unit economics.

items.answer:
For a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd choose **Apollo + HubSpot** for the best balance of AI prospecting, sequencing, CRM, and cost. If UK/EU data compliance is your highest priority, choose **Cognism or Dealfront for data**, then use a controlled outreach tool such as **Lemlist** rather than relying on an autonomous AI SDR.

## Best platforms

| Platform | Best for | Strengths | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Apollo.io** | Best all-in-one startup option | Prospect database, AI research, enrichment, sequences, dialer, CRM integrations, affordable entry point | US-based provider; you must review international transfers, source provenance, and lawful-basis documentation |
| **Cognism** | Highest-confidence UK/EU prospect data | Strong UK and European coverage, phone verification, TPS/CTPS and other do-not-call screening, privacy and DSAR processes | Usually quote-based and more expensive; still requires a separate CRM and engagement workflow |
| **Dealfront** | Europe-first and EU-hosted prospecting | European company data, website visitor identification, intent signals, public-register sourcing, EU-focused privacy posture | Less suitable if you need a fully built-in multichannel outbound engine |
| **Lemlist** | Compliant, personalized outbound execution | Email sequences, AI personalization, multichannel workflows, DPA, EEA data storage according to its documentation | It is primarily an engagement layer, so data quality depends on your data provider |
| **Clay** | Advanced enrichment and custom AI workflows | Connects multiple data providers, supports AI research and personalization, highly flexible | Compliance depends on every connected data source and subprocessor; not ideal as the first tool for a team with no SDR process |
| **Outreach or Salesloft** | Mature enterprise sales operations | Strong governance, sequencing, analytics, coaching, and CRM controls | Generally excessive cost and complexity for a 20-person startup without SDRs |

Apollo documents UK/EU notices, opt-out controls, DPA terms, data-subject workflows, and the ability to exclude EU contacts from prospecting and emailing. That makes it a practical startup choice, but not an automatic legal solution. [knowledge.apollo](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409141087757-General-Data-Protection-Regulation-GDPR-Overview)

Cognism states that it screens telephone data against UK TPS/CTPS and other national do-not-call lists, performs privacy assessments, supports DSARs, and maintains GDPR-related documentation. Dealfront states that it uses a legitimate-interest basis for business contact data and provides a DPA, while positioning itself around European data sources. [help.cognism](https://help.cognism.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406236439826-What-has-Cognism-done-internally-to-comply-with-GDPR-and-data-privacy-regulations)

## My recommended stack

### Option 1: Best overall

**Apollo + HubSpot CRM + Google Workspace/Microsoft 365**

Use Apollo to identify accounts, find contacts, generate research briefs, and run small, carefully targeted sequences. Keep HubSpot as the system of record for lifecycle stages, suppression lists, replies, opportunities, and unsubscribe status.

This is the simplest option when nobody has yet built an SDR process. Start with a small number of high-fit accounts rather than immediately sending thousands of emails.

### Option 2: Best for UK/EU compliance

**Dealfront or Cognism + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Dealfront when EU hosting, European company data, and source traceability matter most. Use Cognism when verified UK/EU phone data and country-specific telephone screening are especially important. Send campaigns through Lemlist, whose documentation describes a GDPR DPA and EEA storage. [lemlist](https://www.lemlist.com/de/legal/dpa)

This stack costs more and involves more integrations, but it separates **data quality** from **outreach execution**, making vendor and compliance reviews clearer.

### Option 3: Best for sophisticated personalization

**Cognism or Apollo + Clay + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Clay only after your ICP, messaging, suppression rules, and review process are working. It is powerful for combining firmographic, technographic, hiring, funding, and website signals, but every connected provider must be assessed individually; Clay's DPA does not make all external data sources compliant by itself. [explore.openli](https://explore.openli.com/privacy/clay-3/data-processing-agreements)

## GDPR and UK outreach requirements

"GDPR-compliant platform" does not mean every campaign sent through it is lawful. Your company remains responsible for the purpose, lawful basis, targeting, message, retention, and handling of objections.

For UK campaigns, the ICO says that marketing to corporate subscribers by email generally does not require PECR consent, but you still need a valid UK GDPR lawful basis—often legitimate interests—and must distinguish corporate subscribers from sole traders and certain partnerships. The ICO also says legitimate interests is not automatic: you must complete the three-part test and comply with other marketing laws. [ico.org](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)

For EU campaigns, document a legitimate-interest assessment, explain who you are and why you are contacting the person, provide an immediate objection/unsubscribe method, minimize stored data, and maintain a suppression list. The EDPB describes legitimate interest as requiring a legitimate purpose, necessity, and a balancing test against the individual's rights. [edpb.europa](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-adopts-opinion-on-processors-guidelines-on-legitimate-interest-statement-on-draft_en)

## Minimum operating controls

Before sending, configure:

- Country and subscriber-type rules, especially for sole traders and individual professionals.
- A documented legitimate-interest assessment for each campaign or market.
- Vendor DPA, subprocessor list, international-transfer mechanism, retention terms, and deletion process.
- Source and collection date for each contact.
- Privacy notice link or first-touch transparency wording.
- One-click unsubscribe and a central, permanent suppression list.
- TPS/CTPS screening for UK phone outreach and equivalent national registers where applicable.
- Human approval for AI-generated claims, personalization, and contact selection.
- Conservative limits: for example, start with 20–40 highly relevant new contacts per sender per day and monitor complaints, bounces, and positive replies.

## Final choice

I would shortlist **Apollo**, **Cognism**, and **Dealfront** for evaluation:

1. **Apollo** if budget, speed, and an all-in-one workflow matter most.
2. **Cognism** if UK/EU contact quality and compliance evidence justify a premium price.
3. **Dealfront** if European data residency, public-register sourcing, and intent signals are central.

For your situation, the most sensible pilot is **Apollo + HubSpot for 30 days**, with a compliance review before launch. If Apollo's UK/EU data coverage or legal documentation is not sufficient, move to **Cognism or Dealfront for the data layer** and keep **Lemlist** for controlled execution.

items.snippet:
ospecting stack**. My shortlist would be **Regie.ai, Artisan, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, and Clay**, with the right choice depending on your team size, CRM, channel mix, and tolerance for automation risk.

## Shortlist by operating model
items.answer:
If you're moving off 11x, don't evaluate only "another AI SDR." First decide whether you want **autonomous outbound**, **human-led sales engagement**, or a **modular prospecting stack**. My shortlist would be **Regie.ai, Artisan, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, and Clay**, with the right choice depending on your team size, CRM, channel mix, and tolerance for automation risk.

## Shortlist by operating model

| Option | Best fit | What to evaluate |
|---|---|---|
| **Regie.ai / RegieOne** | Closest replacement if you still want AI-led prospecting | Autonomous prospect discovery, enrichment, personalized outreach, calls, LinkedIn workflows, CRM logging, and human handoff. Regie positions its agents as handling discovery through outreach across multiple channels. [regie](https://www.regie.ai/prospecting-agents) |
| **Artisan** | Direct AI-BDR alternative | Quality of research, email personalization, deliverability, objection handling, meeting booking, and how much human control managers retain. |
| **Apollo** | Cost-conscious teams wanting data plus execution in one platform | Contact-data accuracy in your ICP, sequencing, dialer, enrichment, CRM sync, and total cost. Apollo combines prospecting data and sales engagement rather than requiring several separate tools. [apollo](https://www.apollo.io/) |
| **Outreach** | Larger or process-heavy sales organizations | Governance, forecasting, coaching, deal management, permissions, analytics, and enterprise integrations. Outreach now combines engagement, deal management, forecasting, coaching, and AI agents. [outreach](https://www.outreach.io/product) |
| **Salesloft** | Teams focused on rep execution and manager visibility | Cadences, next-best actions, conversation intelligence, coaching, forecasting, and AI-assisted research. Salesloft's AI agents are designed to prioritize actions, research accounts, identify buyers, and support sellers. [salesloft](https://www.salesloft.com/platform/ai-agents) |
| **Clay + your preferred sequencer** | RevOps teams wanting maximum control and data flexibility | Enrichment waterfalls, signal quality, workflow maintenance, cost per enriched record, and integration with your CRM and engagement tool. Clay supports enrichment from many providers and routing qualified prospects into the sales workflow. [clay](https://www.clay.com/blog/how-to-create-your-own-sales-prospect-list-in-minutes) |

## My practical recommendation

- **Want the closest strategic substitute for 11x:** Pilot **Regie.ai and Artisan**.
- **Want lower cost and faster implementation:** Evaluate **Apollo**.
- **Want to put humans back in control while improving execution:** Evaluate **Salesloft or Outreach**.
- **Have strong RevOps capability and unusual ICP signals:** Build a controlled stack around **Clay**, your CRM, and a sequencer.
- **Have enterprise governance, multiple sales teams, or complex forecasting requirements:** Start with **Outreach and Salesloft**, not a standalone AI SDR.

I would avoid replacing 11x with another black-box agent unless the vendor can show exactly **why each prospect was selected, what data informed the message, when a sequence pauses, and how a rep takes over**.

## Evaluation scorecard

Weight the evaluation around outcomes rather than feature count:

| Category | Suggested weight | Questions to ask |
|---|---:|---|
| Pipeline quality | 25% | Does it create qualified opportunities, not merely replies or meetings? |
| Data quality | 15% | What are email accuracy, role accuracy, firmographic freshness, and duplicate rates in your ICP? |
| Deliverability and compliance | 15% | How does it protect domains, manage opt-outs, respect regional rules, and detect risky sending patterns? |
| CRM and workflow fit | 15% | Does it write cleanly to Salesforce or HubSpot, preserve attribution, and prevent duplicate touches? |
| Control and explainability | 10% | Can managers approve messaging, set guardrails, inspect reasoning, and stop campaigns immediately? |
| Rep and manager usability | 10% | Does it reduce work without creating another queue of bad meetings and exceptions? |
| Economics | 10% | Calculate cost per qualified opportunity and cost per pipeline dollar—not just license price. |

## Run a controlled pilot

Give each finalist the same:

1. ICP and exclusions.
2. Target-account list.
3. Approved positioning, proof points, and disallowed claims.
4. Suppression list and existing customer records.
5. Meeting qualification criteria.
6. Two to four weeks of execution time.

Measure **qualified meetings held, opportunity conversion, pipeline created, positive-reply rate, bounce rate, unsubscribe/complaint rate, rep time required, and CRM-data accuracy**. Require the vendor to report results by segment, persona, message, and channel; otherwise, you won't know whether the tool works or merely found an easy pocket of prospects.

## The key decision

The most important question is: **Are you replacing an SDR, replacing an outbound stack, or replacing a workflow?**

If you need predictable enterprise execution, choose a governed platform such as Outreach or Salesloft. If you need autonomous top-of-funnel coverage, test Regie and Artisan. If you primarily need better targeting and data while keeping your team's process, Apollo or Clay may be the better transition. Claims about AI SDR performance are often vendor-supplied, so make your own pilot results the deciding evidence.

items.prompt: I'm a SDR manager. Best AI sales prospecting and outbound platforms for a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team with GDPR compliance for UK and EU prospect data.
items.snippet:
r; not ideal as the first tool for a team with no SDR process |
| **Outreach or Salesloft** | Mature enterprise sales operations | Strong governance, sequencing, analytics, coaching, and CRM controls | Generally excessive cost and complexit
items.answer:
For a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd choose **Apollo + HubSpot** for the best balance of AI prospecting, sequencing, CRM, and cost. If UK/EU data compliance is your highest priority, choose **Cognism or Dealfront for data**, then use a controlled outreach tool such as **Lemlist** rather than relying on an autonomous AI SDR.

## Best platforms

| Platform | Best for | Strengths | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Apollo.io** | Best all-in-one startup option | Prospect database, AI research, enrichment, sequences, dialer, CRM integrations, affordable entry point | US-based provider; you must review international transfers, source provenance, and lawful-basis documentation |
| **Cognism** | Highest-confidence UK/EU prospect data | Strong UK and European coverage, phone verification, TPS/CTPS and other do-not-call screening, privacy and DSAR processes | Usually quote-based and more expensive; still requires a separate CRM and engagement workflow |
| **Dealfront** | Europe-first and EU-hosted prospecting | European company data, website visitor identification, intent signals, public-register sourcing, EU-focused privacy posture | Less suitable if you need a fully built-in multichannel outbound engine |
| **Lemlist** | Compliant, personalized outbound execution | Email sequences, AI personalization, multichannel workflows, DPA, EEA data storage according to its documentation | It is primarily an engagement layer, so data quality depends on your data provider |
| **Clay** | Advanced enrichment and custom AI workflows | Connects multiple data providers, supports AI research and personalization, highly flexible | Compliance depends on every connected data source and subprocessor; not ideal as the first tool for a team with no SDR process |
| **Outreach or Salesloft** | Mature enterprise sales operations | Strong governance, sequencing, analytics, coaching, and CRM controls | Generally excessive cost and complexity for a 20-person startup without SDRs |

Apollo documents UK/EU notices, opt-out controls, DPA terms, data-subject workflows, and the ability to exclude EU contacts from prospecting and emailing. That makes it a practical startup choice, but not an automatic legal solution. [knowledge.apollo](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409141087757-General-Data-Protection-Regulation-GDPR-Overview)

Cognism states that it screens telephone data against UK TPS/CTPS and other national do-not-call lists, performs privacy assessments, supports DSARs, and maintains GDPR-related documentation. Dealfront states that it uses a legitimate-interest basis for business contact data and provides a DPA, while positioning itself around European data sources. [help.cognism](https://help.cognism.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406236439826-What-has-Cognism-done-internally-to-comply-with-GDPR-and-data-privacy-regulations)

## My recommended stack

### Option 1: Best overall

**Apollo + HubSpot CRM + Google Workspace/Microsoft 365**

Use Apollo to identify accounts, find contacts, generate research briefs, and run small, carefully targeted sequences. Keep HubSpot as the system of record for lifecycle stages, suppression lists, replies, opportunities, and unsubscribe status.

This is the simplest option when nobody has yet built an SDR process. Start with a small number of high-fit accounts rather than immediately sending thousands of emails.

### Option 2: Best for UK/EU compliance

**Dealfront or Cognism + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Dealfront when EU hosting, European company data, and source traceability matter most. Use Cognism when verified UK/EU phone data and country-specific telephone screening are especially important. Send campaigns through Lemlist, whose documentation describes a GDPR DPA and EEA storage. [lemlist](https://www.lemlist.com/de/legal/dpa)

This stack costs more and involves more integrations, but it separates **data quality** from **outreach execution**, making vendor and compliance reviews clearer.

### Option 3: Best for sophisticated personalization

**Cognism or Apollo + Clay + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Clay only after your ICP, messaging, suppression rules, and review process are working. It is powerful for combining firmographic, technographic, hiring, funding, and website signals, but every connected provider must be assessed individually; Clay's DPA does not make all external data sources compliant by itself. [explore.openli](https://explore.openli.com/privacy/clay-3/data-processing-agreements)

## GDPR and UK outreach requirements

"GDPR-compliant platform" does not mean every campaign sent through it is lawful. Your company remains responsible for the purpose, lawful basis, targeting, message, retention, and handling of objections.

For UK campaigns, the ICO says that marketing to corporate subscribers by email generally does not require PECR consent, but you still need a valid UK GDPR lawful basis—often legitimate interests—and must distinguish corporate subscribers from sole traders and certain partnerships. The ICO also says legitimate interests is not automatic: you must complete the three-part test and comply with other marketing laws. [ico.org](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)

For EU campaigns, document a legitimate-interest assessment, explain who you are and why you are contacting the person, provide an immediate objection/unsubscribe method, minimize stored data, and maintain a suppression list. The EDPB describes legitimate interest as requiring a legitimate purpose, necessity, and a balancing test against the individual's rights. [edpb.europa](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-adopts-opinion-on-processors-guidelines-on-legitimate-interest-statement-on-draft_en)

## Minimum operating controls

Before sending, configure:

- Country and subscriber-type rules, especially for sole traders and individual professionals.
- A documented legitimate-interest assessment for each campaign or market.
- Vendor DPA, subprocessor list, international-transfer mechanism, retention terms, and deletion process.
- Source and collection date for each contact.
- Privacy notice link or first-touch transparency wording.
- One-click unsubscribe and a central, permanent suppression list.
- TPS/CTPS screening for UK phone outreach and equivalent national registers where applicable.
- Human approval for AI-generated claims, personalization, and contact selection.
- Conservative limits: for example, start with 20–40 highly relevant new contacts per sender per day and monitor complaints, bounces, and positive replies.

## Final choice

I would shortlist **Apollo**, **Cognism**, and **Dealfront** for evaluation:

1. **Apollo** if budget, speed, and an all-in-one workflow matter most.
2. **Cognism** if UK/EU contact quality and compliance evidence justify a premium price.
3. **Dealfront** if European data residency, public-register sourcing, and intent signals are central.

For your situation, the most sensible pilot is **Apollo + HubSpot for 30 days**, with a compliance review before launch. If Apollo's UK/EU data coverage or legal documentation is not sufficient, move to **Cognism or Dealfront for the data layer** and keep **Lemlist** for controlled execution.

[hackceleration](https://hackceleration.com/labs/best/b2b-prospecting-startups) | Data accuracy and deliverability must be tested for your ICP |

| **Instantly** | High-volume email execution | Sending infrastructure and campaign management at relatively low cost | It is primarily an outreach/sending layer, not a complete prospect database and AI SDR |

## My recommended evaluation order

1. **Apollo.io:** Run a 30–60-day pilot to test list quality, campaign speed, positive replies, qualified meetings, and CRM synchronization.
2. **Reply.io:** Consider it if you want more explicit AI qualification and meeting-booking assistance.
3. **Clay:** Add it only when basic prospecting works but you need deeper enrichment or more personalized workflows.
4. **11x or Artisan:** Evaluate after you have repeatable ICP definitions, messaging, qualification rules, and sufficient pipeline economics.
5. **Instantly:** Consider it when your main need is email sending and domain infrastructure rather than an all-in-one prospecting platform.

## Final recommendation

As a RevOps lead, you're likely looking for a CRM and sales engagement platform that aligns with your company's needs. Amplemarket and 11x are both sales engagement platforms, but they cater to different use cases and team sizes.

**Amplemarket**

Amplemarket is a cold outreach platform that's primarily used for email and LinkedIn messaging. It offers phone and LinkedIn automation, but it's not designed to be a full-fledged CRM. **11x**

Pros:

2. **Integration with multiple platforms**: 11x integrates with a wide range of platforms, including CRMs, marketing automation software, and helpdesk tools.
3. **Customizable automation**: 11x offers advanced automation features, including custom workflows and AI-powered lead scoring.

2. **Higher pricing**: 11x's pricing plans are more expensive than Amplemarket's, especially for larger teams.

**Recommendation**

Considering your 20-person B2B SaaS startup has no SDR team, I recommend **Amplemarket**. Here's why:

1. **Simplified onboarding**: Amplemarket's user-friendly interface makes it easier to onboard new sales teams or users.
2. **Cost-effective**: Amplemarket's pricing plans are more affordable for smaller teams.
3. **Focus on cold outreach**: Amplemarket is specifically designed for cold outreach and lead generation, which aligns with your startup's needs.

Ultimately, it's essential to assess both platforms and determine which one aligns better with your business needs, team size, and growth plans. I recommend scheduling demos for both platforms to get a better understanding of each tool's features and pricing.

- **11x**: The setup process for 11x is reportedly much simpler and faster. It's often completed within a few days, and their integration with popular CRMs like Salesforce is seamless and hassle-free.

11x is a popular online learning platform that offers courses, certifications, and degree programs. While it has its strengths, there are some credibility concerns that buyers (or students) should be aware of:

1. **Lack of Accreditation**: 11x is not institutionally accredited in the United States. This may impact the recognition of their degrees or certifications by employers or other institutions.
2. **No Transparency about Outcomes**: The platform doesn't provide enough information about job placement rates, graduate outcomes, or other metrics that are crucial for potential students to make informed decisions.
3. **Variable Instructional Quality**: The quality of courses and instruction can vary significantly, depending on the instructor or the subject matter.
4. **Self-Directed Learning**: Some courses on 11x are self-directed, which can be beneficial for self-motivated learners, but may not be ideal for students who require more structure or guidance.
5. **Some Courses Lack Industry Relevance**: While 11x offers courses in various fields, some of them might not be up-to-date or relevant to the current industry standards.
6. **Financial Aid and Support**: The platform's financial aid process and support services may not be as comprehensive as those offered by traditional degree-granting institutions.
7. **Limited Interaction with Faculty**: The online format and self-directed nature of some courses might limit interaction with instructors and fellow students.
8. **Course Categorization**: 11x has many different types of educational offerings which, at first glance, can be quite confusing to those who are new to online learning.

To alleviate these concerns, it's essential for buyers (or students) to:

a. Research the courses and programs thoroughly.
b. Read reviews from past students and check their ratings.
c. Verify the credentials of the instructors teaching specific courses.
d. Evaluate the curriculum and course materials to ensure they align with your goals and industry needs.
e. Contact 11x's support services to ask about their financial aid process, student support, and job placement resources.

Ultimately, as with any educational platform, it's crucial to approach 11x with a critical eye and do your due diligence to ensure that it aligns with your goals and expectations.

items.answer:
For a 20-person B2B SaaS startup with no SDR team, I'd choose **Apollo + HubSpot** for the best balance of AI prospecting, sequencing, CRM, and cost. If UK/EU data compliance is your highest priority, choose **Cognism or Dealfront for data**, then use a controlled outreach tool such as **Lemlist** rather than relying on an autonomous AI SDR.

## Best platforms

| Platform | Best for | Strengths | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Apollo.io** | Best all-in-one startup option | Prospect database, AI research, enrichment, sequences, dialer, CRM integrations, affordable entry point | US-based provider; you must review international transfers, source provenance, and lawful-basis documentation |
| **Cognism** | Highest-confidence UK/EU prospect data | Strong UK and European coverage, phone verification, TPS/CTPS and other do-not-call screening, privacy and DSAR processes | Usually quote-based and more expensive; still requires a separate CRM and engagement workflow |
| **Dealfront** | Europe-first and EU-hosted prospecting | European company data, website visitor identification, intent signals, public-register sourcing, EU-focused privacy posture | Less suitable if you need a fully built-in multichannel outbound engine |
| **Lemlist** | Compliant, personalized outbound execution | Email sequences, AI personalization, multichannel workflows, DPA, EEA data storage according to its documentation | It is primarily an engagement layer, so data quality depends on your data provider |
| **Clay** | Advanced enrichment and custom AI workflows | Connects multiple data providers, supports AI research and personalization, highly flexible | Compliance depends on every connected data source and subprocessor; not ideal as the first tool for a team with no SDR process |
| **Outreach or Salesloft** | Mature enterprise sales operations | Strong governance, sequencing, analytics, coaching, and CRM controls | Generally excessive cost and complexity for a 20-person startup without SDRs |

Apollo documents UK/EU notices, opt-out controls, DPA terms, data-subject workflows, and the ability to exclude EU contacts from prospecting and emailing. That makes it a practical startup choice, but not an automatic legal solution. [knowledge.apollo](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409141087757-General-Data-Protection-Regulation-GDPR-Overview)

Cognism states that it screens telephone data against UK TPS/CTPS and other national do-not-call lists, performs privacy assessments, supports DSARs, and maintains GDPR-related documentation. Dealfront states that it uses a legitimate-interest basis for business contact data and provides a DPA, while positioning itself around European data sources. [help.cognism](https://help.cognism.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406236439826-What-has-Cognism-done-internally-to-comply-with-GDPR-and-data-privacy-regulations)

## My recommended stack

### Option 1: Best overall

**Apollo + HubSpot CRM + Google Workspace/Microsoft 365**

Use Apollo to identify accounts, find contacts, generate research briefs, and run small, carefully targeted sequences. Keep HubSpot as the system of record for lifecycle stages, suppression lists, replies, opportunities, and unsubscribe status.

This is the simplest option when nobody has yet built an SDR process. Start with a small number of high-fit accounts rather than immediately sending thousands of emails.

### Option 2: Best for UK/EU compliance

**Dealfront or Cognism + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Dealfront when EU hosting, European company data, and source traceability matter most. Use Cognism when verified UK/EU phone data and country-specific telephone screening are especially important. Send campaigns through Lemlist, whose documentation describes a GDPR DPA and EEA storage. [lemlist](https://www.lemlist.com/de/legal/dpa)

This stack costs more and involves more integrations, but it separates **data quality** from **outreach execution**, making vendor and compliance reviews clearer.

### Option 3: Best for sophisticated personalization

**Cognism or Apollo + Clay + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Clay only after your ICP, messaging, suppression rules, and review process are working. It is powerful for combining firmographic, technographic, hiring, funding, and website signals, but every connected provider must be assessed individually; Clay's DPA does not make all external data sources compliant by itself. [explore.openli](https://explore.openli.com/privacy/clay-3/data-processing-agreements)

## GDPR and UK outreach requirements

"GDPR-compliant platform" does not mean every campaign sent through it is lawful. Your company remains responsible for the purpose, lawful basis, targeting, message, retention, and handling of objections.

For UK campaigns, the ICO says that marketing to corporate subscribers by email generally does not require PECR consent, but you still need a valid UK GDPR lawful basis—often legitimate interests—and must distinguish corporate subscribers from sole traders and certain partnerships. The ICO also says legitimate interests is not automatic: you must complete the three-part test and comply with other marketing laws. [ico.org](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)

For EU campaigns, document a legitimate-interest assessment, explain who you are and why you are contacting the person, provide an immediate objection/unsubscribe method, minimize stored data, and maintain a suppression list. The EDPB describes legitimate interest as requiring a legitimate purpose, necessity, and a balancing test against the individual's rights. [edpb.europa](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-adopts-opinion-on-processors-guidelines-on-legitimate-interest-statement-on-draft_en)

## Minimum operating controls

Before sending, configure:

- Country and subscriber-type rules, especially for sole traders and individual professionals.
- A documented legitimate-interest assessment for each campaign or market.
- Vendor DPA, subprocessor list, international-transfer mechanism, retention terms, and deletion process.
- Source and collection date for each contact.
- Privacy notice link or first-touch transparency wording.
- One-click unsubscribe and a central, permanent suppression list.
- TPS/CTPS screening for UK phone outreach and equivalent national registers where applicable.
- Human approval for AI-generated claims, personalization, and contact selection.
- Conservative limits: for example, start with 20–40 highly relevant new contacts per sender per day and monitor complaints, bounces, and positive replies.

## Final choice

I would shortlist **Apollo**, **Cognism**, and **Dealfront** for evaluation:

1. **Apollo** if budget, speed, and an all-in-one workflow matter most.
2. **Cognism** if UK/EU contact quality and compliance evidence justify a premium price.
3. **Dealfront** if European data residency, public-register sourcing, and intent signals are central.

For your situation, the most sensible pilot is **Apollo + HubSpot for 30 days**, with a compliance review before launch. If Apollo's UK/EU data coverage or legal documentation is not sufficient, move to **Cognism or Dealfront for the data layer** and keep **Lemlist** for controlled execution.

Yes. There are serious, well-documented credibility concerns about 11x (the AI SDR startup) that buyers should treat as red flags. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)

## Core credibility issues

- **Fabricated customer claims and testimonials:** A March 2025 TechCrunch investigation reported that 11x listed companies (e.g., ZoomInfo, Airtable) as customers without authorization and published customer testimonials that were denied by the quoted individuals or companies. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Inflated growth metrics (ARR):** Former employees and sources alleged 11x counted full-year contract value toward annual recurring revenue (ARR) even when customers exercised early "break clauses" and left after ~3 months, making growth look stronger than committed revenue. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Very high early churn:** Multiple sources (former/current employees, industry observers) report ~70–80% of customers churn within the first 3 months; one 2026 review cites ~75% 3-month churn. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Product performance complaints:** Reports include AI "hallucinations," features not working as expected, inconsistent results, and messaging that can feel generic or robotic—leading to more manual work than promised. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Contract rigidity and pricing opacity:** Buyers note a high minimum annual commitment (often cited around $60K), no pilots, opaque pricing until sales conversations, and anxiety around credits/usage visibility. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)

## What this means for a buyer

Because social proof on 11x's site has been called into question, independent verification becomes essential:

- **Do not rely on website logos or case-study quotes** as evidence of fit or performance. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)
- **Require independently sourced customer references** (e.g., find 3 current users via LinkedIn or your network, not just references 11x provides) and ask specifically about 12-month retention, reply quality, and setup effort. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)
- **Pressure-test contract terms** (break clauses, usage caps, data export, termination rights) and get clarity on how performance will be measured and reported. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)

## Bottom line

Given the combination of alleged misrepresentation, high early churn, and mixed product performance reports, 11x is widely characterized in 2025–2026 analyst/review content as a **high-risk purchase** for most teams unless you can independently validate outcomes and secure flexible contractual protections. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)

## How I would deploy it

items.answer:
If you're moving off 11x, don't evaluate only "another AI SDR." First decide whether you want **autonomous outbound**, **human-led sales engagement**, or a **modular prospecting stack**. My shortlist would be **Regie.ai, Artisan, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, and Clay**, with the right choice depending on your team size, CRM, channel mix, and tolerance for automation risk.

## Shortlist by operating model

| Option | Best fit | What to evaluate |
|---|---|---|
| **Regie.ai / RegieOne** | Closest replacement if you still want AI-led prospecting | Autonomous prospect discovery, enrichment, personalized outreach, calls, LinkedIn workflows, CRM logging, and human handoff. Regie positions its agents as handling discovery through outreach across multiple channels. [regie](https://www.regie.ai/prospecting-agents) |
| **Artisan** | Direct AI-BDR alternative | Quality of research, email personalization, deliverability, objection handling, meeting booking, and how much human control managers retain. |
| **Apollo** | Cost-conscious teams wanting data plus execution in one platform | Contact-data accuracy in your ICP, sequencing, dialer, enrichment, CRM sync, and total cost. Apollo combines prospecting data and sales engagement rather than requiring several separate tools. [apollo](https://www.apollo.io/) |
| **Outreach** | Larger or process-heavy sales organizations | Governance, forecasting, coaching, deal management, permissions, analytics, and enterprise integrations. Outreach now combines engagement, deal management, forecasting, coaching, and AI agents. [outreach](https://www.outreach.io/product) |
| **Salesloft** | Teams focused on rep execution and manager visibility | Cadences, next-best actions, conversation intelligence, coaching, forecasting, and AI-assisted research. Salesloft's AI agents are designed to prioritize actions, research accounts, identify buyers, and support sellers. [salesloft](https://www.salesloft.com/platform/ai-agents) |
| **Clay + your preferred sequencer** | RevOps teams wanting maximum control and data flexibility | Enrichment waterfalls, signal quality, workflow maintenance, cost per enriched record, and integration with your CRM and engagement tool. Clay supports enrichment from many providers and routing qualified prospects into the sales workflow. [clay](https://www.clay.com/blog/how-to-create-your-own-sales-prospect-list-in-minutes) |

## My practical recommendation

- **Want the closest strategic substitute for 11x:** Pilot **Regie.ai and Artisan**.
- **Want lower cost and faster implementation:** Evaluate **Apollo**.
- **Want to put humans back in control while improving execution:** Evaluate **Salesloft or Outreach**.
- **Have strong RevOps capability and unusual ICP signals:** Build a controlled stack around **Clay**, your CRM, and a sequencer.
- **Have enterprise governance, multiple sales teams, or complex forecasting requirements:** Start with **Outreach and Salesloft**, not a standalone AI SDR.

I would avoid replacing 11x with another black-box agent unless the vendor can show exactly **why each prospect was selected, what data informed the message, when a sequence pauses, and how a rep takes over**.

## Evaluation scorecard

Weight the evaluation around outcomes rather than feature count:

| Category | Suggested weight | Questions to ask |
|---|---:|---|
| Pipeline quality | 25% | Does it create qualified opportunities, not merely replies or meetings? |
| Data quality | 15% | What are email accuracy, role accuracy, firmographic freshness, and duplicate rates in your ICP? |
| Deliverability and compliance | 15% | How does it protect domains, manage opt-outs, respect regional rules, and detect risky sending patterns? |
| CRM and workflow fit | 15% | Does it write cleanly to Salesforce or HubSpot, preserve attribution, and prevent duplicate touches? |
| Control and explainability | 10% | Can managers approve messaging, set guardrails, inspect reasoning, and stop campaigns immediately? |
| Rep and manager usability | 10% | Does it reduce work without creating another queue of bad meetings and exceptions? |
| Economics | 10% | Calculate cost per qualified opportunity and cost per pipeline dollar—not just license price. |

## Run a controlled pilot

Give each finalist the same:

1. ICP and exclusions.
2. Target-account list.
3. Approved positioning, proof points, and disallowed claims.
4. Suppression list and existing customer records.
5. Meeting qualification criteria.
6. Two to four weeks of execution time.

Measure **qualified meetings held, opportunity conversion, pipeline created, positive-reply rate, bounce rate, unsubscribe/complaint rate, rep time required, and CRM-data accuracy**. Require the vendor to report results by segment, persona, message, and channel; otherwise, you won't know whether the tool works or merely found an easy pocket of prospects.

## The key decision

The most important question is: **Are you replacing an SDR, replacing an outbound stack, or replacing a workflow?**

If you need predictable enterprise execution, choose a governed platform such as Outreach or Salesloft. If you need autonomous top-of-funnel coverage, test Regie and Artisan. If you primarily need better targeting and data while keeping your team's process, Apollo or Clay may be the better transition. Claims about AI SDR performance are often vendor-supplied, so make your own pilot results the deciding evidence.

If you're moving off 11x, don't evaluate only "another AI SDR." First decide whether you want **autonomous outbound**, **human-led sales engagement**, or a **modular prospecting stack**. ## Shortlist by operating model

| **Regie.ai / RegieOne** | Closest replacement if you still want AI-led prospecting | Autonomous prospect discovery, enrichment, personalized outreach, calls, LinkedIn workflows, CRM logging, and human handoff. Regie positions its agents as handling discovery through outreach across multiple channels. [regie](https://www.regie.ai/prospecting-agents) |

Apollo combines prospecting data and sales engagement rather than requiring several separate tools. [apollo](https://www.apollo.io/) |
| **Outreach** | Larger or process-heavy sales organizations | Governance, forecasting, coaching, deal management, permissions, analytics, and enterprise integrations. Outreach now combines engagement, deal management, forecasting, coaching, and AI agents. [outreach](https://www.outreach.io/product) |
| **Salesloft** | Teams focused on rep execution and manager visibility | Cadences, next-best actions, conversation intelligence, coaching, forecasting, and AI-assisted research. Salesloft's AI agents are designed to prioritize actions, research accounts, identify buyers, and support sellers. [salesloft](https://www.salesloft.com/platform/ai-agents) |
| **Clay + your preferred sequencer** | RevOps teams wanting maximum control and data flexibility | Enrichment waterfalls, signal quality, workflow maintenance, cost per enriched record, and integration with your CRM and engagement tool. Clay supports enrichment from many providers and routing qualified prospects into the sales workflow. [clay](https://www.clay.com/blog/how-to-create-your-own-sales-prospect-list-in-minutes) |

## My practical recommendation

- **Want the closest strategic substitute for 11x:** Pilot **Regie.ai and Artisan**.
- **Want lower cost and faster implementation:** Evaluate **Apollo**.
- **Want to put humans back in control while improving execution:** Evaluate **Salesloft or Outreach**.
- **Have strong RevOps capability and unusual ICP signals:** Build a controlled stack around **Clay**, your CRM, and a sequencer.
- **Have enterprise governance, multiple sales teams, or complex forecasting requirements:** Start with **Outreach and Salesloft**, not a standalone AI SDR.

I would avoid replacing 11x with another black-box agent unless the vendor can show exactly **why each prospect was selected, what data informed the message, when a sequence pauses, and how a rep takes over**.

## Evaluation scorecard

Weight the evaluation around outcomes rather than feature count:

| Category | Suggested weight | Questions to ask |
|---|---:|---|
| Pipeline quality | 25% | Does it create qualified opportunities, not merely replies or meetings? |
| Data quality | 15% | What are email accuracy, role accuracy, firmographic freshness, and duplicate rates in your ICP? |
| Deliverability and compliance | 15% | How does it protect domains, manage opt-outs, respect regional rules, and detect risky sending patterns? |
| CRM and workflow fit | 15% | Does it write cleanly to Salesforce or HubSpot, preserve attribution, and prevent duplicate touches? |
| Control and explainability | 10% | Can managers approve messaging, set guardrails, inspect reasoning, and stop campaigns immediately? |
| Rep and manager usability | 10% | Does it reduce work without creating another queue of bad meetings and exceptions? |
| Economics | 10% | Calculate cost per qualified opportunity and cost per pipeline dollar—not just license price. |

## Run a controlled pilot

Give each finalist the same:

1. ICP and exclusions.
2. Target-account list.
3. Approved positioning, proof points, and disallowed claims.
4. Suppression list and existing customer records.
5. Meeting qualification criteria.
6. Two to four weeks of execution time.

Measure **qualified meetings held, opportunity conversion, pipeline created, positive-reply rate, bounce rate, unsubscribe/complaint rate, rep time required, and CRM-data accuracy**. Require the vendor to report results by segment, persona, message, and channel; otherwise, you won't know whether the tool works or merely found an easy pocket of prospects.

## The key decision

The most important question is: **Are you replacing an SDR, replacing an outbound stack, or replacing a workflow?**

If you need predictable enterprise execution, choose a governed platform such as Outreach or Salesloft. If you need autonomous top-of-funnel coverage, test Regie and Artisan. If you primarily need better targeting and data while keeping your team's process, Apollo or Clay may be the better transition. Claims about AI SDR performance are often vendor-supplied, so make your own pilot results the deciding evidence.

| **Dealfront** | Europe-first and EU-hosted prospecting | European company data, website visitor identification, intent signals, public-register sourcing, EU-focused privacy posture | Less suitable if you need a fully built-in multichannel outbound engine |
| **Lemlist** | Compliant, personalized outbound execution | Email sequences, AI personalization, multichannel workflows, DPA, EEA data storage according to its documentation | It is primarily an engagement layer, so data quality depends on your data provider |
| **Clay** | Advanced enrichment and custom AI workflows | Connects multiple data providers, supports AI research and personalization, highly flexible | Compliance depends on every connected data source and subprocessor; not ideal as the first tool for a team with no SDR process |
| **Outreach or Salesloft** | Mature enterprise sales operations | Strong governance, sequencing, analytics, coaching, and CRM controls | Generally excessive cost and complexity for a 20-person startup without SDRs |

Apollo documents UK/EU notices, opt-out controls, DPA terms, data-subject workflows, and the ability to exclude EU contacts from prospecting and emailing. That makes it a practical startup choice, but not an automatic legal solution. [knowledge.apollo](https://knowledge.apollo.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409141087757-General-Data-Protection-Regulation-GDPR-Overview)

Cognism states that it screens telephone data against UK TPS/CTPS and other national do-not-call lists, performs privacy assessments, supports DSARs, and maintains GDPR-related documentation. Dealfront states that it uses a legitimate-interest basis for business contact data and provides a DPA, while positioning itself around European data sources. [help.cognism](https://help.cognism.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406236439826-What-has-Cognism-done-internally-to-comply-with-GDPR-and-data-privacy-regulations)

## My recommended stack

### Option 1: Best overall

**Apollo + HubSpot CRM + Google Workspace/Microsoft 365**

Use Apollo to identify accounts, find contacts, generate research briefs, and run small, carefully targeted sequences. Keep HubSpot as the system of record for lifecycle stages, suppression lists, replies, opportunities, and unsubscribe status.

This is the simplest option when nobody has yet built an SDR process. Start with a small number of high-fit accounts rather than immediately sending thousands of emails.

### Option 2: Best for UK/EU compliance

**Dealfront or Cognism + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Dealfront when EU hosting, European company data, and source traceability matter most. Use Cognism when verified UK/EU phone data and country-specific telephone screening are especially important. Send campaigns through Lemlist, whose documentation describes a GDPR DPA and EEA storage. [lemlist](https://www.lemlist.com/de/legal/dpa)

This stack costs more and involves more integrations, but it separates **data quality** from **outreach execution**, making vendor and compliance reviews clearer.

### Option 3: Best for sophisticated personalization

**Cognism or Apollo + Clay + HubSpot + Lemlist**

Use Clay only after your ICP, messaging, suppression rules, and review process are working. It is powerful for combining firmographic, technographic, hiring, funding, and website signals, but every connected provider must be assessed individually; Clay's DPA does not make all external data sources compliant by itself. [explore.openli](https://explore.openli.com/privacy/clay-3/data-processing-agreements)

## GDPR and UK outreach requirements

"GDPR-compliant platform" does not mean every campaign sent through it is lawful. Your company remains responsible for the purpose, lawful basis, targeting, message, retention, and handling of objections.

For UK campaigns, the ICO says that marketing to corporate subscribers by email generally does not require PECR consent, but you still need a valid UK GDPR lawful basis—often legitimate interests—and must distinguish corporate subscribers from sole traders and certain partnerships. The ICO also says legitimate interests is not automatic: you must complete the three-part test and comply with other marketing laws. [ico.org](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/)

For EU campaigns, document a legitimate-interest assessment, explain who you are and why you are contacting the person, provide an immediate objection/unsubscribe method, minimize stored data, and maintain a suppression list. The EDPB describes legitimate interest as requiring a legitimate purpose, necessity, and a balancing test against the individual's rights. [edpb.europa](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/news/edpb-adopts-opinion-on-processors-guidelines-on-legitimate-interest-statement-on-draft_en)

## Minimum operating controls

Before sending, configure:

- Country and subscriber-type rules, especially for sole traders and individual professionals.
- A documented legitimate-interest assessment for each campaign or market.
- Vendor DPA, subprocessor list, international-transfer mechanism, retention terms, and deletion process.
- Source and collection date for each contact.
- Privacy notice link or first-touch transparency wording.
- One-click unsubscribe and a central, permanent suppression list.
- TPS/CTPS screening for UK phone outreach and equivalent national registers where applicable.
- Human approval for AI-generated claims, personalization, and contact selection.
- Conservative limits: for example, start with 20–40 highly relevant new contacts per sender per day and monitor complaints, bounces, and positive replies.

## Final choice

I would shortlist **Apollo**, **Cognism**, and **Dealfront** for evaluation:

1. **Apollo** if budget, speed, and an all-in-one workflow matter most.
2. **Cognism** if UK/EU contact quality and compliance evidence justify a premium price.
3. **Dealfront** if European data residency, public-register sourcing, and intent signals are central.

For your situation, the most sensible pilot is **Apollo + HubSpot for 30 days**, with a compliance review before launch. If Apollo's UK/EU data coverage or legal documentation is not sufficient, move to **Cognism or Dealfront for the data layer** and keep **Lemlist** for controlled execution.

items.prompt: Are there any credibility concerns a buyer should know about 11x?
items.snippet: A March 2025 TechCrunch investigation reported that 11x listed companies (e.g., ZoomInfo, Airtable) as customers without authorization and published customer testimonials that were denied by the quoted individuals or companies. [techcrunch]
items.answer:
Yes. There are serious, well-documented credibility concerns about 11x (the AI SDR startup) that buyers should treat as red flags. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)

## Core credibility issues

- **Fabricated customer claims and testimonials:** A March 2025 TechCrunch investigation reported that 11x listed companies (e.g., ZoomInfo, Airtable) as customers without authorization and published customer testimonials that were denied by the quoted individuals or companies. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Inflated growth metrics (ARR):** Former employees and sources alleged 11x counted full-year contract value toward annual recurring revenue (ARR) even when customers exercised early "break clauses" and left after ~3 months, making growth look stronger than committed revenue. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Very high early churn:** Multiple sources (former/current employees, industry observers) report ~70–80% of customers churn within the first 3 months; one 2026 review cites ~75% 3-month churn. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Product performance complaints:** Reports include AI "hallucinations," features not working as expected, inconsistent results, and messaging that can feel generic or robotic—leading to more manual work than promised. [techcrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have/)
- **Contract rigidity and pricing opacity:** Buyers note a high minimum annual commitment (often cited around $60K), no pilots, opaque pricing until sales conversations, and anxiety around credits/usage visibility. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)

## What this means for a buyer

Because social proof on 11x's site has been called into question, independent verification becomes essential:

- **Do not rely on website logos or case-study quotes** as evidence of fit or performance. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)
- **Require independently sourced customer references** (e.g., find 3 current users via LinkedIn or your network, not just references 11x provides) and ask specifically about 12-month retention, reply quality, and setup effort. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)
- **Pressure-test contract terms** (break clauses, usage caps, data export, termination rights) and get clarity on how performance will be measured and reported. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)

## Bottom line

Given the combination of alleged misrepresentation, high early churn, and mixed product performance reports, 11x is widely characterized in 2025–2026 analyst/review content as a **high-risk purchase** for most teams unless you can independently validate outcomes and secure flexible contractual protections. [thecroreport](https://thecroreport.com/tools/11x/)
